solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Too much publicly displayed male chest

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public view
the male pronoun
the top of the body, where the chest sits; also a garment covering it

explanation.surface: A man baring his chest in public is going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of a flasher; the clue splits into three short pieces read in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-the-top is an idiom for excessive or exaggerated behaviour.

clue.text: (& 5dn.) Rather doubtful ex-PM should get a stretch

parts.note: Earl Grey was British Prime Minister in the 1830s
a stretch of land is an area

explanation.surface: A dodgy former prime minister ought to be sent to prison for a stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stretch' suggests a prison term, but it is an expanse of ground. Earl Grey, of the tea, was Prime Minister 1830-34.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is an unclear situation; the definition works as an adjective-like phrase for something of uncertain status.

clue.text: Boris, broken with age, loveless — a minor TV character

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put together differently
love is zero in tennis, a round letter, so being without love means dropping that letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson, worn down by age and unloved, is reduced to a bit-part on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O (a zero score in tennis), so the O comes out of BORIS before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Ears is Noddy's elderly friend in the children's TV series, a supporting character.

clue.text: see 18dn.
see 2dn.
Maybe it's Hitler's elect circles restricting its uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising up means the word reads from bottom to top
restricting means hemming in, so one group of letters is held inside the other
going round in circles churns things about, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hitler's chosen people surround and suppress its rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wartime song claiming Hitler had only one ball; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The old song 'Hitler has only got one ball' makes a lone testicle Hitler's, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Grieve over being pressed by Brian, Brenda?

indicators.note: something pressed by another is squeezed between it, so it ends up enclosed

parts.note: Private Eye calls Prince Charles Brian, and he is the Queen's son

indicators.note: to be over is to be turned or knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mourning is weighed upon by Brian, and the question is whether Brenda is the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye's nicknames: Brenda is the Queen and Brian is Prince Charles, so Brian stands for her son.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is Private Eye's name for Queen Elizabeth II, a reigning monarch, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Establishment also contrived Cameron's end

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a name is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of Cameron

explanation.surface: The Establishment also engineered David Cameron's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a business such as a hair or beauty parlour, an establishment in the sense of a shop.

clue.text: Sting finally breaking into crap song

indicators.note: breaking into a place means getting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: dire is slang for very poor quality

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the last letter of Sting

explanation.surface: The singer Sting at last turns up in a rubbish song.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting the musician makes 'song' look like part of the scene, but only his last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament for the dead.

clue.text: Speechifier Miliband upset with one demanding benefit?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Ed Miliband, former Labour leader
someone claiming state benefit is a claimer

explanation.surface: An orator: Ed Miliband, cross, alongside someone on welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' suggests Miliband is annoyed; it only flips his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A declaimer is someone who speaks rhetorically and at length, a speechifier.

clue.text: Complaint from guy pissed with Labour's extremes

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Labour

explanation.surface: A drunk Labour supporter is moaning about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; here it is an illness. Pissed is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The lurgy is British slang for an unspecified minor illness, and a complaint is an ailment.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) "It makes one spit — no alternative — taking on that wardrobe disaster", Brenda describing Kate?

definitions.note: the definition is the phrase that would describe Kate, then pregnant

indicators.note: with no means something is taken away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: an expectorant is a medicine that brings up phlegm
or is the word offering an alternative
clothes moths eat holes in stored clothes
Private Eye's Brenda is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen, quoted on a fashion blunder that made her spit, comments on the Duchess of Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OR from EXPECTORANT leaves EXPECTANT. Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, and ER her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Middleton was pregnant when this appeared, so a woman expecting a baby describes her.

clue.text: (see 21dn.)
Regards exercise as early sign of being a chronic wanker?

definitions.text: early sign of being a chronic wanker?

parts.note: to regard is to look at, to eye
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Someone thinks working out is the first symptom of compulsive self-abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the schoolboy myth that masturbation makes you go blind.
explanation.definitionFit: The old myth says self-abuse ruins the sight, so tired, aching vision would be its first symptom.

clue.text: Pisspoor, leaderless House, Clegg chiefly makeshift

indicators.note: without a leader means the front letter is dropped

parts.note: piss-poor is slang for very bad
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

indicators.note: chiefly points to the head, the opening letter of the name

parts.note: the first letter of Clegg

explanation.surface: A useless, leaderless Commons with Nick Clegg largely improvising.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc means arranged for the occasion only, improvised, which is what makeshift describes.

clue.text: Commons spy who's keen to get commission

parts.note: the House of Commons
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A mole in the Commons wants a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commission' suggests a bribe or a job for the spy; it is the estate agent's fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A house agent is an estate agent, paid by a percentage commission on each property sold.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Examinations entailing bites round penis detailed

indicators.note: entailing means involving or including, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a bite is a snack, a small meal

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: slang for penis

explanation.surface: A medical check involving bite marks on a mangled penis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough; split as de-tailed it cuts the last letter. 'Round' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicals are physical check-ups by a doctor, examinations of a person's health.

clue.text: Say someone did something bad, screwing up time

indicators.note: screwing something up twists it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of wrongdoing, getting the timing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwing up' looks like a phrase; only 'screwing' signals, and 'up' joins the letters being moved.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to attribute blame or a fault to someone, often unfairly.

clue.text: Was on manoeuvres with females, so removed from board?

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A soldier off on exercises with women, and therefore dropped from the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a board of directors; it is a plank of wood with a piece cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece cut away from a plank with a saw has been sawn off it.

clue.text: (& 4dn.) Green, jumped-up sort demands a parliamentary enforcer for each paparazzo

parts.note: a whip keeps party MPs voting in line
per means for each
a snapper is a photographer

explanation.surface: An upstart Green Party member wants a whip to control every paparazzo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the party; it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an impudent, inexperienced young person, a green upstart.

clue.text: Got pissed about … Arsenal?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily; toped is the past tense

explanation.surface: Arsenal fans got drunk over the match result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arsenal' wants to be the football club; it is a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of arms, one example of a depot, a storage place for supplies.

clue.text: Throb near to crack that's odious

indicators.note: to crack is to break apart, so these letters split and regroup

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pulsing sensation close to breaking point is nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means hateful or repugnant, which is what odious means.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) Screwing, end together, clutching article as far as one can

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so a word is gripped inside the others
screwing twists things around, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the definite article

explanation.surface: Having sex and climaxing together while holding onto a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'end together' open after their first two letters to take in THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To the nth degree is an idiom for to the utmost extent, as far as is possible.

clue.text: Top off, "old boy" freed, Kurt Cobain gyrates with hard-on, as a show-starter

indicators.note: to gyrate is to whirl about, so the remaining letters spin into a new order
with its top taken off, the opening letter is removed
freed means let go, so those letters are released from the name

parts.note: taken as written
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
an erection is up

explanation.surface: A shirtless Kurt Cobain dances suggestively on stage to open the gig.
explanation.walkthrough: First the K goes, then the O and B, and what is left of the Nirvana singer's name is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtain up is the moment a theatre performance begins, so it starts the show.

clue.text: see 24ac.
(& 23dn.) Pissed with Cable's balancing act support?

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: Vince Cable, drunk, props up the coalition's delicate balancing act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like Vince Cable the Lib Dem minister; it is a heavy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope walker's act is a balancing feat performed on a taut rope, which holds the performer up.

clue.text: "Horizontal knee-trembler" covers intercourse

indicators.note: the outer words cover, that is contain, the answer spread across them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A sexual position, the knee-trembler done lying down, counts as intercourse.
explanation.walkthrough: A knee-trembler is British slang for sex standing up. 'Intercourse' in its old sense means conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercourse in its original sense means communication or dealings between people, which includes conversation.

clue.text: After U-turn, sod all to protect uranium power plant

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it all round, so other letters go inside
a turnabout on the road sends you back the way you came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sod all is British slang for nothing
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: After a policy reversal, nothing is done to guard a uranium power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uranium power plant' reads as a nuclear station, but the last word is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flowering plant with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Not on the staff unleashed on prick

parts.note: unleashed means let loose, free
to lance is to pierce or prick

explanation.surface: A sacked employee lets fly at a prat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prick' looks like an insult; it is the verb to pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works independently for several clients rather than being a salaried employee.
